title: Proof of Life and Suspension of Payments on Income Annuities
content:
Ashgrove Income Annuities installments are suspended when the company cannot be sure the payment is due to a living payee at a valid address. The provisions below state when a certificate of existence is asked for, what suspends payments, what clears a suspension and what follows.

**Certificate of existence.** From the contract anniversary on or after an annuitant's attained age reaches the tier's proof-of-life age, Ashgrove requests a certificate of existence every proof-of-life interval of the tier. When the certificate is not returned within the tier's response period of the request, payments are suspended.

**Other grounds of suspension.** Payments are also suspended:

- when a payment is returned undeliverable and no valid instructions are on file; and
- when a report of death is received that is not yet confirmed by a certified death certificate.

**Held installments.** *No longer in force:* installments falling due while suspended were held and earned no interest where the tier's figure for interest on suspended payments is "no" — this clause has been superseded by the current basis and is no longer in force.

**Clearing a suspension.** A suspension is cleared only by the record that resolves it:

| Ground of suspension | Record that clears it |
|---|---|
| Certificate of existence overdue | A completed certificate of existence signed by the annuitant and dated after the request |
| Payment returned undeliverable | Confirmed new payment instructions |
| Unconfirmed report of death, not confirmed within the tier's death report verification period | The annuitant's own certificate of existence |

Once cleared, the schedule resumes and the held installments are released in one sum within the tier's held payment release period in business days. A returned payment is reissued by the tier's reissue method for returned payments once instructions are confirmed.

**Suspension ending in death.** *No longer in force:* when the suspension ended in a confirmed death instead, held installments falling due on or before the date of death were released to the estate or survivor and those falling due after it were forfeited — this clause has been superseded by the current basis and is no longer in force.

*Hypothetical case.* A certificate of existence is requested on 1 March with a 60-day response period; it is not returned, and payments are suspended. A certificate later returned, signed by the annuitant but dated 15 February, does not clear the suspension, because it is not dated after the request; one dated 20 May does.

superseded_clauses: Installments falling due while suspended are held and earn no interest when suspended_payments_earn_interest is false.

When the suspension ends in a confirmed death instead, held installments falling due on or before the date of death are released to the estate or survivor and those falling due after it are forfeited.
